NCIS 2026: Connecting Climate Ambition with Capital

RE.Think in London for two days of investor roundtables on financing Africa’s energy transition.

RE.Think Energy Team·11–13 Mar 2026·3 min read

This article is placeholder demonstration copy generated to preview how a From the Field event write-up reads on the site. Replace with real, reviewed event reporting before publishing.

Photo to come
Photo to come

RE.Think travelled to London for NCIS 2026 to connect climate ambition with the investors and partners who can fund it. Across two days of closed-door roundtables and open panels, the conversation centred on what it actually takes to move African energy assets from a promising pipeline to a closed deal.

Where we contributed

Our team hosted a roundtable on structuring blended-finance vehicles that let concessional capital absorb early-stage risk, freeing private investors to come in once a project is bankable rather than speculative. We also met one-on-one with a number of institutional investors actively building out their Africa allocation for the first time.

What we took away

NCIS reinforced that global capital is ready to move — what is missing on many projects is still the early, unglamorous work of de-risking and structuring. That is exactly the gap RE.Think exists to close, and the conversations in London gave us several concrete leads to follow up on with partners and projects in the coming months.
